sections.label: CPF flexibility and MediSave changes
sections.summary: Provides advance applications for lump-sum Retirement Account withdrawals, automatic Retirement Sum Scheme payouts at 70, and full MediSave Basic Healthcare Sum changes from 1 January 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: First, provide CPF members with the flexibility to make advance applications for a lump-sum withdrawal from their Retirement Account upon reaching their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Second, allow payouts under the Retirement Sum Scheme to begin automatically upon the member reaching 70 years of age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Third, fully effect the MediSave changes relating to the introduction of the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) which took effect from 1 January 2016.

sections.label: Automatic Retirement Sum Scheme payouts
sections.summary: About one in three members are expected to benefit from automatic starting of payouts under the Retirement Sum Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: About one in three members are expected to benefit from the automatic starting of payouts under the Retirement Sum Scheme.

sections.label: Lump-sum withdrawal at Payout Eligibility Age
sections.summary: Members may withdraw up to 20% of their Retirement Account after reaching Payout Eligibility Age, 65 years old for most members.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, members will now have the flexibility to make a lump-sum withdrawal of up to 20% of their Retirement Account after reaching their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA), 65 years old for most members.

sections.label: Flexibility and automatic payouts at 70
sections.summary: The speaker hopes CPF Board can be more flexible and is glad CPF payouts will start automatically when members reach age 70.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For situations like these, I hope CPF Board can be more flexible.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also glad that CPF payouts will start automatically when members reach age 70.

sections.label: Fixed BHS and lump-sum withdrawal
sections.summary: BHS for each cohort will be fixed, avoiding a rising Minimum Sum, and amendments allow lump-sum withdrawal of up to 20% of the Retirement Account at 65.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Better peace of mind is because BHS for each cohort will be fixed, so that people do not have to worry about a constantly rising Minimum Sum ‒ a "moving target".

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments will also allow Singaporeans to make a lump-sum withdrawal of up to 20% of their Retirement Account upon reaching 65 years old.

sections.label: Transfer to related person's MediSave
sections.summary: New section 18D allows transfer of a member's Ordinary Account or Special Account monies to the MediSave Account of a related person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The new section 18D allows the transfer of a member's monies standing in his Ordinary Account or Special Account to the MediSave Account of a related person.

sections.label: CPF Review Panel withdrawal flexibility
sections.summary: The CPF Review Panel allowed withdrawal of up to 20% of Retirement Account savings at PEA, with lower monthly payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The CPF Review Panel, in its report in early 2015, said it recognises that many members may have short-term cash flow needs in retirement, and came up with the flexibility to allow members to withdraw up to 20% of their Retirement Account savings, but only at PEA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The illustrative table provided in the same CPF Review Report shows that members who opt for a 20% lump-sum withdrawal at PEA will stand to receive $10 to $100 lesser in monthly payouts depending on the amount standing in their Retirement Accounts.

sections.label: CPF withdrawal before PEA
sections.summary: The CPF Review Panel's recommendation was right but should allow withdrawal after age 55 and before PEA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The CPF Review Panel has made the right recommendation to allow members the flexibility to withdraw up to 20% of their Retirement Account savings, but it has fallen short by restricting the option to exercise this flexibility only when members attain their PEA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: There should be an option for members to exercise such withdrawal after age 55 and prior to reaching PEA.

sections.label: Temasek negative shareholder returns
sections.summary: Temasek Holdings announced negative 9% shareholder returns for the 2016 financial year, causing public debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In July this year, Temasek Holdings announced that in the 2016 financial year, shareholder returns came in at a negative 9%, stirring up much public debate.

sections.label: Board recovery of erroneous payments
sections.summary: Sections give the Board wide powers to recover cash grants or payments paid in error, and ask about safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 14, subsection 3A to 3D, and section 14, subsection 4A provide wide-ranging powers to the Board to recover cash grants or payments which were paid in error to the person's account.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Page: 55 What are the safeguards to ensure that the recovery of payment or grant paid in error is also not erroneously done as no legal proceedings can be instituted on such recovery?

sections.label: Ordinary Account transfer related persons
sections.summary: The passage asks who are the related persons a member can transfer money to from his or her Ordinary Account.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Who are the related persons that a member can transfer money from his/her Ordinary Account to?

sections.label: Board payouts without application
sections.summary: The board will be allowed to start payouts for members on the Retirement Sum Scheme without requiring applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The board will now be allowed to start payouts for members on the Retirement Sum Scheme, without requiring members to make an application.

sections.label: Support for BHS and MediSave
sections.summary: The speaker supports implementing BHS and amendments removing the requirement to top up the MediSave Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Page: 56 Secondly, I support the implementation of BHS and the amendments to remove the requirement to top up the MediSave Account.

sections.label: Section 18D family fund transfers
sections.summary: The speaker commends flexibility for family members to transfer funds to MediSave Accounts and asks what terms and conditions the Board may impose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, on the proposed new section 18D, I commend the greater flexibility granted to family members, allowing them to transfer funds from their Ordinary and/or Special Accounts to the MediSave Accounts of their family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The flexibility and freedom granted by this amendment will lighten the anxiety of members in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, can the Minister clarify what exactly are the "terms and conditions as the Board may impose", as specified in section 18D?

sections.label: Singapore CPF ranking weakened
sections.summary: The Melbourne Mercer Global Pension Index shows Singapore's CPF ranking weakened in recent years due to a decline in adequacy rating.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Melbourne Mercer Global Pension Index, the ranking of Singapore's CPF has weakened in recent years because of a decline in the rating for adequacy.

sections.label: Extra interest promotes adequacy
sections.summary: Extra interest on the initial part of combined balances, set at $60,000, and on initial balances of those aged 55 and above has promoted better adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In recent years, the extra interest on the initial part of an account holder's combined balances, currently set at $60,000, as well as on the initial balances of those aged 55 and above, has significantly promoted better adequacy.

sections.label: Recovery of lump sums, CPF vision
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether legislation allows recovery of incorrectly dispensed lump-sum withdrawals and what the CPF Board's long-term vision is.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I would like to clarify if the legislation allows for lump-sum withdrawals which have been incorrectly dispensed to be recovered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, I would like to ask the Minister what the long-term vision of CPF Board is on managing individual and collective responsibility for retirement needs is.

sections.label: Deferring payouts to age 70
sections.summary: The amendments let Retirement Sum Scheme members defer payout start up to age 70, allowing a longer runway of payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the amendments, it also means members in the Retirement Sum Scheme can defer the start of their payouts up to the age of 70, which would allow Page: 59 for a longer runway of payouts for their retirement.

sections.label: CPF lump-sum withdrawal option
sections.summary: The amendments include an option for CPF members to make a lump-sum withdrawal from the Retirement Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendments this time round also include the option for CPF members to make a lump-sum withdrawal from the Retirement Account.

sections.label: CPF Act transfers between spouses
sections.summary: Amendments to the CPF Act in the last round allowed transfers between married couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For instance, the amendments to the CPF Act in the last round allowed transfers between married couples.

sections.label: Scam risk for seniors
sections.summary: The Member is concerned that senior citizens will become an even more prominent target for scams after age 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the lump-sum withdrawal now an option, I am concerned that senior citizens will become an even more prominent target for scams after the age of 65.

sections.label: Housing schemes supplement retirement income
sections.summary: Singaporeans with plans for withdrawn money should be prepared to cash in on their homes using schemes like Lease Buyback or Silver Housing Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singaporeans who have plans for the money they have withdrawn should then be prepared to cash in on their homes, with schemes like the Lease Buyback scheme or Silver Housing Bonus to fall back on to supplement their income for the rest of their life.

sections.label: Lump-sum withdrawal and financial counselling
sections.summary: A key amendment allows eligible members born in 1958 or later to withdraw up to 20% from their Retirement Accounts at 65, with hopes for CPF financial counselling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some, like her, have made a conscious choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But there are many others who may not be aware of the options and they keep on struggling when they should retire and enjoy some quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For many Singaporeans who do not have excess money or assets, your property and retirement account would be what you live on in your twilight years, so you would have to be financially savvy and manage your money with caution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the end, I do hope that CPF Board would have some financial counselling or collaterals to advise members on the implications of making lump-sum withdrawals and what it means for the members' future payouts and what are the other options they can undertake to supplement their retirement income for the rest of their life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A key amendment today is to allow a lump-sum withdrawal of up to 20% from eligible members' Retirement Accounts when they reach 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This option will be available to those born in 1958 or later.

sections.label: Transfers to family MediSave Accounts
sections.summary: Transferring Ordinary or Special Account monies to family members' MediSave Accounts lets recipients benefit from extra interest and move closer to CPF LIFE plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By allowing the transfer of monies in either or both of the member's Ordinary Accounts and Special Accounts to the MediSave Accounts of their family members who have lower balances, the recipients can benefit from the extra interest on lower balances and enjoy a higher effective interest rate overall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the long term, they will be closer to having their own CPF LIFE plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This amendment will benefit family members who are not working or are engaged in lower paying jobs for a variety of reasons – to look after the family, illness or disability.

sections.label: Advisory Panel withdrawal cap recommendation
sections.summary: The Advisory Panel recommended a well-balanced cap of 20% on early withdrawal, including amounts withdrawn at age 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At the end of the day, the Advisory Panel's recommendation is a well-balanced one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: They recognised that some people may need to withdraw the money earlier but there should be a cap of 20%, including the amount withdrawn at the age of 55.

sections.label: Automatic payout start at 70
sections.summary: The proposal sets the automatic start for payout at the age of 70.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: What we are proposing is, basically, to set the automatic start for the payout at the age of 70.

sections.label: Case-by-case further deferment allowed
sections.summary: Further deferment would be allowed case by case if the member is convinced of the trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On a case-by-case basis, we would allow for further deferment, provided that we are convinced that the member knows what the trade-offs are.

sections.label: Family members for top-ups
sections.summary: Family members include spouses, siblings, parents, grandparents, parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The family members would include not just spouses but also siblings, parents, grandparents, parents-in-law and grandparents-in-law.

sections.label: No father-in-law to son-in-law top-up
sections.summary: A father-in-law cannot directly top up the son-in-law's MediSave Account, as policy encourages younger generations topping up older generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If you ask me whether a father-in-law can directly top up the MediSave Account for the son-in-law this way, the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have a general policy for the transfer of CPF savings where we would like to encourage the younger generations to top up the CPF account for the older generations and not the other way round.

sections.label: Feedback on simplified explanations
sections.summary: Based on feedback, about 90% found the simplified ways of explanation useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Based on feedback, about 90% of them found the simplified ways of explanation useful.

sections.label: CPF retirement planning consultation
sections.summary: CPF Board invites members nearing 55 for face-to-face consultations and sends pamphlets at age 54 about retirement planning options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: They invited CPF members, just before they turn 55, to come to CPF Board for a one-to-one, face-to-face consultation where CPF Board staff will try to explain to them what are the options, what are the decisions and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Thus, starting from October this year, starting this month, CPF Board will send information pamphlets to all members at age 54.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: CPF Board will also send invites to a target group on this retirement planning service before they turn 55, so that they are aware of this optional service available to them.
